audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart disagreed with itself and with the packet: row 0 said Karma while whys[0] said the lane favours you, and row 4 said Karma while the mirror audit (karma__warwick) flipped row 4 to Warwick on both layers.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is [Warwick, Skill, Warwick, Skill, Warwick, Warwick, Warwick] at 56.5% over 1023 games; the mirror explicitly records row 4 as Warwick.
audit.corrected: Rows 0 and 4 flipped to Warwick on both layers as one atomic group, with ratings raised to match. Row 3 left alone: the mirror did not flag it and I will not introduce an unmirrored flip.

audit.why: Spikes are keyed correctly: levels 3-5 pattern, level 6 Infinite Duress, Blade of the Ruined King first item, two-item side lane. Only the level 6 spike's mechanical description was wrong, corrected under point 4.
audit.corrected: Spike timings left as-is; spikes[1].text rewritten for accuracy.

audit.whatIsWrong: Infinite Duress described as a 'point-and-click fight starter' in phases[4].why, breakdown.late and whys[4], and spikes[1].text claimed it 'locks her out of casting' Mantra.
audit.why: Riot's text: Warwick leaps in a direction and suppresses the FIRST champion he collides with for 1.5s, and the kit flags R as a channel — interruptible, any CC cancels it. So it can miss, and Karma's Focused Resolve root or Mantra-empowered root can cut it short.
audit.corrected: Restated as a directional leap onto the first champion collided with, 1.5s suppression, cancellable by CC — so commit after she has spent Focused Resolve (12s cooldown at every rank), not before.

audit.why: Focused Resolve is a flat 12s at all ranks, so the punish window is fixed and does not shrink with rank — the existing 'engage on its cooldown' framing holds.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet flagged 'E's Primal Howl' in spikes[3].text as a probable wrong ability name.
audit.why: False positive — Primal Howl IS Warwick's E. The fear displacement genuinely can pull you out of Focused Resolve's tether range.

edits.before: Infinite Duress is a point-and-click fight starter that locks his carry tool. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Karma's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Infinite Duress leaps and suppresses the first champion it collides with for 1.5s — it can miss, and her root cancels the channel. Bait it out, then commit.

edits.before: Infinite Duress is a point-and-click fight starter that locks his carry tool — build your teamfight around that. Karma carry threat: 6/10 — shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.
edits.after: Infinite Duress leaps onto the first champion it collides with for a 1.5s suppress — pick your line, because CC cancels the channel. Karma carry threat: 6/10 — shift to picks if she gets ahead.

edits.before: Your R suppress locks her out of casting the RW mantra root, and since she has no dash you can flat run her down the moment she uses her shield defensively.
edits.after: Your R leaps onto the first champion it hits and suppresses 1.5s — it can miss, and CC cancels the channel, so fire it after she has spent Focused Resolve, not into it.

edits.before: At 6 your R suppress denies her mantra root and kills her.
edits.after: At 6 your R leap suppresses 1.5s if it lands — bait her root.

notes: Row 3 (Levels 4-5) disagrees with the packet chart (packet says Skill, both layers say Warwick) but the mirror audit did not flag it, so I left the pair untouched rather than introduce an unmirrored flip. Focused Resolve is a flat 12s cooldown at every rank — worth using that number in future rewrites. Text throughout this matchup refers to Karma as 'he'; I corrected pronouns only inside strings I was already editing, since a pronoun-only edit is under the 25-char skip threshold in some fields and would burn edits elsewhere.
